description: We are AstroKuskat, a team of engineering students from El Salvador fueled by a bold vision: to put Central America on the global map of planetary exploration. Uniting our expertise across engineering, we unlock the potential of Central America's nature by providing a vital, unrecognized testing ground to validate the next generation of Artemis missions. We are not just solving a challenge; we are claiming Central America's place in humanity's journey to the stars and beyond.
summary:
What if the next step toward the Moon begins in Central America?
AstroKuskat is an interactive geospatial platform that identifies and characterizes six volcanic sites across Central America as potential terrestrial analogs for lunar exploration. Using open data from NASA and other scientific sources, our platform connects these landscapes with specific lunar regions through interactive 3D/2D visualization and a nine-variable environmental analysis framework.
Rather than simply identifying visual similarities, AstroKuskat evaluates both the potential and limitations of each analog site, providing a scientifically grounded tool to support exploration planning, geological research, and the testing of technologies relevant to future Artemis missions.
details:
Before future lunar missions can reach the Moon, technologies and operational concepts must be tested in terrestrial analog environments. While several analog sites are recognized worldwide, Central America's volcanic corridor remains largely unexplored despite offering diverse terrain, volcanic structures, and geological features relevant to planetary exploration. AstroKuskat highlights this potential by identifying and evaluating six sites across the region as possible lunar analogs.

HOW ASTROKUSKAT WORKS

AstroKuskat evaluates Central American volcanic sites against their lunar counterparts through NASA datasets, geospatial analysis, and a nine-variable evaluation framework.

WHAT MAKES ASTROKUSKAT DIFFERENT

Unlike traditional analog catalogs that focus on visual similarity, AstroKuskat evaluates where an analog works, where it falls short, and how those differences impact Artemis-relevant testing.

ENVIRONMENTAL EVALUATION FRAMEWORK

For every Earth–Moon pair, our team evaluated and visualized them across nine environmental variables.

DATA AND TOOL RESOURCES

  • NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) & Geosciences Node: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Mission Data Archive (LOLA, LROC, Mini-RF) and LRO Diviner Lunar Radiometer Experiment (DLRE) Archive.
  • NASA Earth Observation & Climate: NASA Earthdata Search, NASA Worldview (MODIS Land Surface Temperature), and NASA Langley Research Center (LaRC) POWER Data Access Viewer.
  • NASA Lunar Reference: NASA Science (Weather on the Moon)
  • We used Devin (as an AI engineering assistant for code) for development workflows in Visual Studio Code, Google Gemini for research and data gathering, Nano Banana for image generating and Microsoft Copilot for writing, editing, and translating the project details.
  • Web Infrastructure & Domain: GoDaddy (custom domain registration and DNS management for the website)
  • Frontend Development & Libraries: HTML (page structure), CSS with Tailwind CSS (visual design), and JavaScript (interactivity and analog data management), integrated with Leaflet (2D map), globe.gl via Three.js and WebGL (3D globe), and Font Awesome (icons).

INTENDED IMPACT

Applications for Artemis

  • 🧑‍🚀 EVA Training
  • 🌋Geological Field Training
  • 🚙 Rover Mobility Testing
  • 🏠 Habitat Deployment
  • 🔧 Hardware Testing

Regional Impact

  • 🎓 STEM Development
  • 🌎 International Collaboration
  • 🚀 Space Ecosystem Visibility

FUTURE EXPANSION

AstroKuskat was designed as a scalable geospatial framework. Future developments include expanding the catalog with additional analog sites across Central America, integrating interactive 3D terrestrial terrain visualization, incorporating new evaluation parameters, and adding accessibility and distance analyses to support multi-site testing campaigns and operational planning.
